tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has received a communication from the Directorate General of GST Intelligence (DGGI), Belagavi Zonal Unit, regarding alleged ineligible availment of Input Tax Credit (ITC) on services availed in connection with its Initial Public Offering (IPO) during FY 2021-22 to 2023-24 and 2024-25. The authority has indicated that such expenses relate to the issue of shares, which is considered a non-GST supply, and has advised payment of tax, interest, and penalty aggregating to ₹3,44,89,344 and ₹4,36,78,720 or submission of a representation by 27.08.2025. The Company is in the process of examining the matter and will take appropriate action in due course.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company had challenged additions made under the assessment order passed under Section 143(3) read with Section 263 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, including alleged excess stock of ₹11,14,72,010 and prior-period income of ₹4,48,21,141. The Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals)-2, Panaji, vide appellate order dated 30 June 2026, partly allowed the Company's appeal. The addition of ₹3,60,16,402 towards alleged excess stock and the addition of ₹4,48,21,141 towards prior-period income were deleted. However, the addition of ₹7,54,55,608 towards alleged excess stock, taxable at the special rate under Section 115BBE of the Income-tax Act, 1961, was sustained. The Company has already discharged tax at the normal rate and is evaluating the appellate order to consider appropriate legal remedies.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Central Circle-1, Mangalore. The appeal was decided by the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals)-2, Panaji.
tax_litigation.status: Aggrieved by the order of the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals)-2, Panaji, the Company has filed an appeal before the Hon'ble Income Tax Appellate Tribunal, Bangalore, on 5 August 2026, challenging the sustained addition of ₹7,54,55,608 towards alleged unexplained investment under Section 69B of the Income-tax Act, 1961, read with Section 115BBE. The tax effect involved in the appeal is ₹3,28,68,463. The appeal is pending adjudication before the Tribunal.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company had challenged the Order-in-Original dated 30 April 2024, which confirmed the demand relating to alleged undervaluation and misdeclaration of imported fish meal, along with differential customs duty, interest, redemption fine and penalties. The Company and three other appellants filed appeals before CESTAT.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Commissioner of Customs, Mangalore. The appeals were decided by the Hon’ble Customs, Excise & Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT), Bangalore Regional Bench.
tax_litigation.status: Vide Final Order Nos. 20934–20937/2026 dated 24 June 2026, the Hon’ble CESTAT set aside the Order-in-Original and the entire demand of customs duty of ₹15,24,30,536, along with unquantified interest, redemption fine and penalties. The Tribunal held that the Department had failed to establish undervaluation with cogent evidence and allowed all four appeals with consequential relief. The Company may seek a consequential refund of ₹75,00,000 appropriated under the Order-in-Original, subject to the applicable statutory procedure. The matter stands decided in favour of the Company, subject to any further appeal or proceedings initiated by the Department.
